short: His Confessions and City of God shaped Western Christian theology for over a millennium.
full:
Born in Roman North Africa in 354, Augustine studied rhetoric, drifted through Manichaeism and Neoplatonism, and taught in Rome and Milan before converting to Christianity in 386 under the influence of Ambrose. He returned to Africa, was ordained, and became bishop of Hippo Regius in 395, a position he held for the rest of his life while producing an enormous body of theological and philosophical writing.

His Confessions, an unprecedented autobiographical examination of his own conversion, and City of God, written after the sack of Rome in 410 to answer pagan claims that abandoning the old gods had caused the empire's ruin, became foundational texts of Western Christianity. His arguments on original sin, grace and predestination framed theological debate for the following thousand years. He died in 430 as the Vandals besieged Hippo, one of the last major intellectual figures of the Western empire.
